findings.description: contractArtifactPaths treats any exports value containing '/' as a local filesystem path unless it matches node:/npm:/URL schemes. A future exports value that re-exports an EXTERNAL package (e.g. "./fp": "lodash/fp" or "./x": "@scope/pkg") would be resolved as <pkgDir>/lodash/fp, making the smoke gate FATAL on a fully built tree with a misleading 'build first' message. Scanned all 42 workspace packages: ZERO such values exist today, so there is no live false positive. The bare-name skip (!s.includes('/')) only rejects values WITHOUT a slash, which is the inverse of the risky shape.
findings.fix_sketch: Reject values that do not start with './', '../', or '/' (relative-path contract) in addition to the existing node:/npm:/URL and bare-name skips; keep exports['./package.json'] working since it starts with './'. Add a unit case for '@scope/pkg' and 'dep/subpath'.

findings.description: Concurrent executions of verify-exports (two smoke gates running simultaneously in a shared checkout) race inside attw's --pack path. Observed empirically during review: running old + new verify-exports concurrently (zsh process substitution) produced WRONG, disjoint violation sets (5 vs 4 violations on totally different packages, all spurious); the same two binaries run sequentially are byte-identical, exit 0, publint 30 / attw 23. The gate now runs this preflight on every smoke run, so two concurrent smoke runs can spuriously fail. Pre-existing tooling property (attw/npm pack temp-state collision), not introduced by this commit, but amplified by the gate's mandatory scope.
findings.fix_sketch: Do not fix in this change (pre-existing). Mitigation options for later: serialize the preflight with a lock file, or document that concurrent smoke runs in one checkout are unsupported. File a backlog item.
